## 2. Project Purpose

### Problem Statement
> {Who has the problem, what is the problem, what does it cost them currently.
> Max 3 sentences. This should be specific — not "the current system is outdated"
> but "the current invoicing process requires 4 hours of manual data entry per week
> and produces ~12% error rate, costing the finance team roughly N hours in corrections."}

### Proposed Solution
> {What this project will build or change, at a high level.
> Not a feature list — a one-paragraph description of the solution approach.}

### Strategic Alignment
> {Which organizational goal, OKR, or strategic initiative this project supports.
> For personal/solo: learning goal, market hypothesis, or similar.}

## 3. Scope

### In Scope
- {Deliverable or workstream 1}
- {Deliverable or workstream 2}
- {Deliverable or workstream 3}

### Out of Scope (Explicit Exclusions)
- {What will NOT be built or addressed in this project — be specific}
- {Common trap: if stakeholders might assume something is included, list it here as excluded}

### Scope Boundary Statement
> {One sentence that draws the hard line: "This project covers X up to and including Y.

## 4. Objectives & Success Criteria

### Business Objectives
| # | Objective | Measurement | Target | By When |
|---|-----------|-------------|--------|---------|
| 1 | {e.g. Reduce invoice processing time} | {Hours/week manual entry} | {<1hr/week} | {Launch + 30d} |
| 2 | {e.g. Improve data accuracy} | {Error rate %} | {<2%} | {Launch + 60d} |
| 3 | {e.g. Enable self-serve onboarding} | {Support tickets/month} | {-40%} | {Q2 2026} |

### Definition of Done (Business Level)
> {What "this project is complete" looks like at the business level — the acceptance condition
> the sponsor will use to confirm the project is done. Not a feature list.}
>
> Example: "The new billing system is live, processing 100% of transactions without the legacy
> system running in parallel, and the finance team lead has confirmed the error rate is within
> acceptable range."

- {KPI 1: metric, current baseline, target}
- {KPI 2: metric, current baseline, target}

## 9. Constraints & Assumptions

### Constraints (Fixed — Cannot Be Changed)
| # | Constraint | Impact if violated |
|---|-----------|-------------------|
| 1 | {e.g. Must launch before [date] — contractual} | {e.g. Penalty clause triggers} |
| 2 | {e.g. Budget capped at $X} | {e.g. Scope must be cut} |
| 3 | {e.g. Must use existing AWS infrastructure} | {e.g. Restricts tech choices} |

### Assumptions (Believed True — Not Yet Verified)
| # | Assumption | Owner to verify | Verification method | Risk if wrong |
|---|-----------|----------------|---------------------|---------------|
| 1 | {e.g. Client API will be documented and available by Week 2} | {PM / Tech Lead} | {API access granted} | {High — blocks development} |
| 2 | {e.g. Design Figma files delivered before sprint 2} | {PM} | {File received in Figma} | {Medium — delays frontend} |
| 3 | {e.g. No breaking database schema changes in existing system} | {Tech Lead} | {DB audit in discovery phase} | {High — migration needed} |

**Rule:** If an assumption is violated, it becomes an issue (logged in `docs/dev-docs/KNOWN-ISSUES.md`)
and may trigger a change request (per the change control process in `docs/pm/CHANGE-LOG.md`).

## 10. Authority & Decision Rights

| Decision type | Authority | Escalation path |
|--------------|-----------|-----------------|
| Feature scope additions | {PM + Sponsor approval} | {Client sign-off if external} |
| Budget changes (within contingency) | {PM} | — |
| Budget changes (>contingency) | {Sponsor} | {Finance / Board if >$X} |
| Technology architecture changes | {Tech Lead + PM} | {Sponsor for significant changes} |
| Timeline extensions | {PM + Sponsor} | {Client if external} |
| Project suspension or cancellation | {Sponsor} | {Board / leadership if program-level} |
| Acceptance of deliverables | {Client contact / Sponsor} | — |

**PM authority statement:** The Project Manager is authorized to make day-to-day decisions
within the approved scope, budget, and timeline. Decisions outside these boundaries require
sponsor approval before action is taken.
